chunks: And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from some of his freedmen, who said:

I asked him about the nocturnal emission of the fasting person. He said: 'If he emits semen during the day in the month of Ramadan, he should not sleep until he performs ghusl. And if he becomes junub at night in the month of Ramadan, he is not allowed to sleep for a moment until he performs ghusl. So whoever becomes junub in the month of Ramadan and sleeps until morning, upon him is freeing a slave or feeding sixty poor people, and making up that day, and he completes his fasting, and it will never catch up to him (i.e., it does not count as the obligatory fast for that day).'
ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for sleeping before ghusl after nocturnal emission during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific fiqh of nocturnal emission (ihtilam) during Ramadan, distinguishing between daytime and nighttime occurrences. It establishes that sleeping while junub until dawn incurs a major kaffarah (freeing a slave or feeding sixty poor) alongside qada, a ruling derived from the principle that the state of impurity invalidates the day's fast if it persists into morning. The text emphasizes the urgency of performing ghusl to restore ritual purity and ensure the validity of the remaining fast.
